side_table.row_heights_note: Which statement decides the five drawn row heights on the cell_stack family (side_rows; side_bar_left also used cell_stack until 2026-09-29 and now draws the two-column cell_grid). 'reference' follows the factory reference 世荣.pdf - cell_qty taller, the other four equal - which is the delivered behaviour and the default. 'artwork' follows base.pdf's own five tiles: each cell is drawn at its own source height at the frame scale, giving Q.TY : others = 1.765 with a 1.268 spread across the other four, which is what the template happened to produce. Both are kept: 'reference' is the reading taken from the factory mark, 'artwork' is the template's own proportions, and which one production should ship is not settled by measurement alone. Only the drawn numbers change - the region band and the owner's order are the same either way. See the round docs/rounds/20260917-003-side-table-row-ratio.md.
side_table.rule: the cell_stack band is apportioned by weight - cell_qty qty_row_ratio units, the other four one unit each - and each cell is drawn to fill its slot, so the drawn row heights are exactly Q.TY : others = qty_row_ratio : 1 with the others equal. This is the row_heights='reference' path; row_heights='artwork' ignores qty_row_ratio and cuts the band evenly, letting each tile size itself
side_table.evidence: Measured on the factory reference 世荣.pdf, all 20 pages x 2 side faces (40 faces). In the single-column five-cell form (12 faces: p5, p13-p17, aspect h/w 0.784-1.070) Q.TY / mean(other four) = 1.4886, 1.4887, 1.4889, 1.4900, 1.4902, 1.4922, 1.4926 twice each (the two side faces of a page repeat), and max/min of the other four rows <= 1.0025 on every face - i.e. equal to within +-0.15 pt, which is the drawing's own quantisation. The ratio is a row-span, not a constant: the same file shows 2.1637 (three-column form, 6 faces) and 2.1667-2.1694 (two-column form, 16 faces) and 1.8219-1.8245 (two-column, uneven row counts, 4 faces), because Q.TY spans N row heights there. 1.489 is the value for the five rows in one column, which is what side_rows and side_bar_left draw.
side_table.note: Drawing each tile at its own source height (128.5 / 66.1 / 83.8 / 70.7 / 70.6 pt) gives 1.765 with a 1.268 spread across the other four, which is what the template happened to produce. Apportioning the slots by qty_row_ratio reproduces the reference's 1.489 and flat instead. The layout_audit info_cells group was written for the flat reading; it now accepts a declared taller Q.TY row when the placement geometry shows that shape, and still reports an unstructured spread.
side_table.mechanism: Q.TY's height is a row span, not a constant: same-column rows give 1.489 (this block), two/three-column forms give 2.167/2.164 and a two-column uneven-row form gives 1.822, because Q.TY spans N row heights there. Only side_rows and side_bar_left draw five rows in one column, so 1.489 applies to them. side_owner_grid puts the five cells in two columns and does not go through cell_stack, so it is unaffected and still draws the tiles' own heights (1.765 ratio, 1.268 spread).
side_table.label_note: Owner 2026-09-29 (factory photos 507021, 557962, 556102 + '黑框框就一点点', 'QTY等标志也可以跟着变大', '单位和品名装箱数这些一起放大，这些字符一起定个规则'; approved '可以，就按这样来'). label_block='template_share': a widened cell keeps its black label block at base.pdf's own share of the cell width (0.335-0.343; factory photos 0.33-0.37) - only the black columns beside the word widen (atlas.measure_label_padding). 'fixed' is the drawing before 2026-09-29 (block at the tile scale, only the white interior widens, block ~0.12 of the cell). label_word='block_share': per cell, every word - label, unit (PCS/cm/kg), Q.TY digits, NAME value - grows by one factor g >= 1 set by the label word: the label keeps its base.pdf share of the block width (0.55-0.78; factory 0.54-0.79) and no word is taller than label_word_max_row_share of its row (base.pdf 0.32-0.38; factory 0.30-0.36; 0.5 is the owner's 'can be bigger', not a factory value). Per cell, not one factor for the table: kg is already 0.42 of its row in base.pdf and would hold every label to 1.2x. A long NAME wraps/shrinks by its own rules. 'fixed' keeps every word at the tile scale.

barcode.max_x_note: UNCAPPED BY OWNER DECISION 2026-08-26. max_x_mm is null, so the symbol scales with its layout slot without an upper bound. What the cap used to do: GS1 General Specifications put the EAN/UPC magnification ceiling at 200% (X = 0.660 mm) because a scan must cross the whole symbol plus both quiet zones in one pass, and an oversized symbol can exceed the scanner's field of view - it is a read limit, not a print limit. Removing the cap does NOT make the symbol unbounded: it now fills whatever slot the layout family gives it, so the ceiling moved from the specification to the page. For reference, the uncapped sweep that originally motivated the cap reached X = 3.917 mm (1187%) on a 1300 mm face and 1.540 mm (467%) on the 900 mm trolley carton. Exceeding warn_above_x_mm is now reported as a non-blocking diagnostic (barcode_above_gs1_ceiling) instead of being silently shrunk. Physical scan verification on a printed sample is the only thing that can confirm a large symbol still reads.
barcode.source: GS1 General Specifications: nominal X 0.330 mm; retail POS 80-200% (0.264-0.660 mm); general distribution 150-200% (0.495-0.660 mm)
barcode.known_pre_existing_deviation: the golden Kmt Style v1 artwork truncates bar height to about 54% of the GS1 nominal height for its magnification; this adaptive policy preserves that inherited proportion and does not worsen it, but it is not GS1-preferred and is reported as a diagnostic
barcode.warn_above_note: Reference only, not a cap. Field evidence that trade practice already exceeds it: the zhuhai 2026-08-14 sheet prints its side-face EAN-13 at X = 1.112 mm (337%), while the front face on the same sheet stays at 0.593 mm (180%). See docs/wide-face-column-layout-evidence-20260824.md.
